pressure.title: A dry mist that condenses where it is needed
pressure.description: Compressed air through a venturi atomises oil into a very fine mist (≈ 1–3 µm) at a low header pressure (≈ 2–5 kPa). The mist travels without settling; at each bearing a reclassifier fitting (small orifice) makes the droplets coalesce so they wet the rolling elements. The slight positive pressure also keeps moisture and dust out of the housing. Oil use is very low and bearing life typically improves; drains and headers are sloped so condensed oil returns or is collected.

script.narration: This module introduces the Oil Mist Lubrication System.
An oil mist system lubricates many pump and motor bearings from one generator.

Compressed air through a venturi atomises oil into a very fine mist (≈ 1–3 µm) carried at low pressure through a header and drop legs; reclassifier fittings at each bearing coalesce the mist into droplets that wet the bearings.
The slight positive pressure keeps contaminants out.
Typical applications include refinery and petrochemical pump fields; electric motors and standby equipment (preservation).

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Process Pump 1 (ball-bearing housing), Process Pump 1 (ball-bearing housing) — Shaft & Coupling (turning), Process Pump 2 (ball-bearing housing), Process Pump 2 (ball-bearing housing) — Shaft & Coupling (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Oil Mist Lubrication System.
Check console alarms and oil level.
Check drain bottles / reclassifiers.
Service console; clean header.
Watch for loss of mist: console alarm. Common cause: air failure, empty reservoir.
Watch for dry bearing: high temperature. Common cause: plugged reclassifier.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
